notes.title: Emote Wheel Update!
notes.content:
Hey Squirrels!

The Emote Wheel Update is here!
Today we're introducing emotes for all squirrels! 
The new emotes are usable via the new Emote Wheel!  

New feature: Emote Wheel!
This new feature allows you to communicate with your fellow squirrels through 8 new emotes, which can all be selected through the Emote Wheel.   

Example: You want to wave to a fellow squirrel:
[olist]
Press and hold Q, 

Select the waving emote (highlighted in the screenshot below)

You'll now be waving excitedly!
[/olist]
It's that easy!


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145962/821c0ee0190a7abcc6e292c3aac26f2e09a0c5ea.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145962/81b28899f37af2e33ccf43a2c13acd9f41340b6b.jpg"]

Feel free to ask any question about this new feature in the Squirreled Away Discord. 


Patch Notes:
v. 1.1.3

Emote-Wheel added

Midsummer event ended

Flower crown added (see below)

Squirreled Away is now Steam Deck Verified!
 
Flower Crown

The squirrels have packed up the midsummer celebration. While the event has ended, we've added the Flower Crown back as a permanent feature.  

Equip the Flower Crown by interacting with the Flower Wreath

Un-equip the Flower Crown by interacting with a Flower Wreath again.  

You can find the Flower Wreath in the building menu under "Decorations". 
Please note you'll need to re-equip the Flower Crown if you exit the game or start a new park.   

  [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145962/0d156221dd502e84e4492f513ffec0a8b8602438.jpg"]

So, enjoy emoting to your fellow squirrels, and have a great Squirreling day!  



The Far Seas team 



PS. If you're enjoying the game, please consider leaving a review for Squirreled Away here on Steam! Thank you!

notes.title: Telly-porter Update!
notes.content:
Hey Squirrels!

The Telly-porter Update is here!
Today we're introducing the Telly-porter and adding performance improvements!  

New feature: Telly-porter!
This new utility item enables you to transport between any two places where a Telly-porter is built. 

Example:
[olist]
Place a Telly-porter in your cozy squirrel home and place another one in a different part of the park (ie. an area with beautiful pink trees, as seen below).

Adjust the telly-porter to show the channel matching the location you want to go to. 

Jump into the Telly-porter to instantly travel to the other location.
[/olist]
Easy as that! 



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145962/74005f7bcb0e4765e795b5cf4a4f8a1412f09162.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145962/166c0e0c7886f47e68f6f4b302c548f0ebf8da3b.jpg"]

To make it easier to know where you'll end up, the Telly-porter shows the location on the screen.  Each Telly-porter also has a number, which matches the channels you can tune into. 

In the example above, the Telly-porter in the house is number 1, and the Telly-porter in the area with the pink trees is number 3, so setting the channel to 3 will take you to where Telly-porter 3 is located. 

The required materials to build the Telly-porter are:
4x Glass Shard 
1x Spring 
3x Plank 
2x Bent Nail
Mediate on these materials to unlock it!   

Feel free to ask any question about this new feature in the Squirreled Away Discord. 


Performance updates!
We've improved the performance of the main menu. This will significantly lower the CPU and GPU usage while using (or idle in) the main menu. 

New default graphics settings are added for the Steam Deck, which will significantly improve performance for Steam Deck users. 

If you're currently playing Squirreled Away on Steam Deck and would like to switch to the new graphics settings, simply head into the Menu -> Graphics -> Reset to Default (small button next to the graphics quality settings).

If the button isn't visible for you, it means you're already on the default settings, and you're good to go!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145962/c71cb8daa6b0e2494e6c6102b3e390080c19ed19.png"]We encourage you to leave feedback on this or any other parts of the game in the Squirreled Away Discord. 

Patch Notes:
v. 1.1.2

Telly-porter added

Main menu is now more performant

New default graphics settings for Steam Deck

"Take me to the River" achievement fixed

Various minor UI fixes.




So, enjoy Telly-porting around the park, and have a great Squirreling day!  



The Far Seas team 



PS. If you're enjoying the game, please consider leaving a review for Squirreled Away here on Steam! Thank you!

notes.title: Squirreled Away - Summer Update!
notes.content:
Hey Squirrels!

Midsummer's here! 
We're celebrating by bringing a midsummer-themed update with new items, decorations, features and fixes!

New Items: Flower Crown and Midsummer Pole
- We've added some items inspired by Swedish midsummer celebrations, that we hope you will have fun with! See if you can find the midsummer pole in the park and equip the flower crown!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145962/dad6d224d7e076eabca766c6f2fc81a1c7f94889.jpg

New Feature: Build with materials from chests
- This means that you can now store all your crafting materials in chests in your favorite house or burrow, and use the materials to build and craft even when you're not near the chest. You'll no longer need to bring all the crafting materials with you in your inventory.

notes.title: Squirreled Away Demo Update!
notes.content:
Hello Squirrels! 

We've made a lot of improvements to the game since launch. Today we're bringing that love to the demo with an update that brings the demo up to par with the full game. We hope players trying out the game will enjoy the improved experience.
And all progress in the demo now carries over directly to the full game! So have fun, and if you get the full game, all your work will be there to keep playing.

Full Game Patch Notes 
Demo Saves will carry over into the full game!
         
 Demo Patch Notes v1.1
✨ New Additions 
 Full Button Remapping! Customize your controls exactly how you like them. 

 Park Renaming! Second thoughts on your park’s name? Change it anytime! 
🔄 Changes
 The Start Menu has been refreshed!

 More Save Slots! Extra room for all your parks and creations. 

 Added shadows to placement highlights when building to help with depth perception. 

 Introduced a new Egg Chair and Sticks in a Jar decoration.  

 Quest descriptions have larger text and can now be scrolled using the mouse wheel or the right thumbstick on a controller. 

 Updated some controller icons for better clarity.

 Mineable resin chunks will now respawn, and you'll find more of them scattered throughout the world.
🐞 Bug Fixes
 Fixed a crash when quitting the game when windows were still loading. 

 Built windows and doors now load properly during startup, reducing temporary performance drops. 

 Fixed Steam Deck resolution issues. 

 Quest log squirrel icons now correctly match their colors in Squirrel Vision. 

 Claire is now properly in focus during her dialogues. 

 Walls now rebuild correctly after demolishing doors and windows. 

 The "Jump" mound no longer respawns after reloading the game. 

 Fixed multiple acorn branches spawning on top of each other. 

 Fixed squirrel animation blending issues 

 Fixed camera collision with water surfaces. 

 Fixed an issue where the camera could clip underwater. 

 Resolved main menu issues with credits unexpectedly exiting the game. 

 Improved controller/mouse focus interactions in menus. 

 Fixed so that the 'Back' button in various menus can now be properly clicked using the mouse. 

 All building blocks are now visually highlighted when hovered over. 

 Various bugs related to player camera and controller behavior during building mode have been addressed.

Improved UI readability on 16:10 aspect ratio screens, particularly for Steam Deck users.

Corrected a minor visual issue with an icon.

 Fixed an issue where sanctuary restoration rewards and achievements could be missed if the player quit during the animation. 

 Language selection is now available on first-time startup when using a controller. 

 Fixed an issue that allowed players to craft duplicate tools at the workbench. 

 The health bar now updates properly after sleeping. 

 The menu can no longer be opened during the intro cutscene. 

 Various landscape improvements. 

 Resolved several audio-related issues.

 Golden Acorn pillars now correctly show collected acorns. 

 Fixed players getting stuck in floors when loading in. 

 Fixed issue with stacking pillars/beams in the same spot 

 No more blocked windows and doors! We’ve cleared out those pesky walls getting in the way of your view. 

 Fixed a bug where climbing wasn’t functioning properly with controllers. 

 Inverted Y-axis setting will now be persistent between loadings. 

 We squashed a bug that made the interact prompt act up when respawning or using "Unstuck." Now it’ll behave itself! . 

 Bushes now have even occlusion settings. No more weird clipping!  

 Floating resin, mushrooms, and clovers? Gone! They’re back on solid ground.. 


That was a lot, but now the demo is even more enjoyable!

Thank you for your interest in Squirreled Away, and have a great Squirreling day!

notes.title: Creative Mode Challenge – Create, Share, Win!
notes.content:
Hey Squirrels! 🐿️


We’ve just launched Creative Mode for Squirreled Away, where you can build to your heart’s content without gathering resources or crafting items! To celebrate, we’re hosting a community challenge where your creativity takes center stage.


The Challenge:
Dive into Creative Mode and let your imagination go wild! 

Design the coziest burrow, the quirkiest treehouse, or whatever your squirrel heart desires. Share your creation in our official Discord for a chance to win a free game key. Perfect for inviting a friend to join the fun!


How to Enter:
1️⃣ Build something amazing in Creative Mode.

2️⃣ Capture it with a screenshot or short video.

3️⃣ Share it on social media, tag us @squirreledgame, and use #SquirreledAway! 

	 You can also post it in the #creative-challenge channel on the Squirreled Away Discord! (Join the Squirreled Away Discord here!) 


⏳ Deadline
Submit your entries by June 10th, 2025. 

After all submissions have been sent in, the community votes on their favorite creations! 


Prizes


The five most creative squirrels will win:



- A free game key!

- New unique and exclusive Discord role!

- Bragging rights



Ready, set… CREATE! 🐿️💨





PS. If you are enjoying Squirreled Away, don't forget to leave a review here on Steam!

notes.title: Creative Mode is out now!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145962/ece719a46fe38077902b51b8c4b0354c987e0106.png
Hey Squirrels! 🐿️

We’ve been absolutely overwhelmed (in the best way!) by your incredible support and feedback since Squirreled Away launched. While our previous updates mostly focused on squashing bugs and quality-of-life tweaks, we’ve been secretly working on two of your most-requested features, Creative Mode and Remappable Controls.

And today’s the day they finally arrive!

Creative Mode: Build Without Limits!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145962/fc650f4795efc02fa079454bf81cba580bae5825.png
We’ve loved seeing how you’ve used the build tools in Squirreled Away to create your cozy homes up in the trees, but now we’re taking it to the next level! Say goodbye to gathering and building restrictions and say hello to pure, unfiltered creativity.

Jump into Creative Mode and choose from these three starting templates:


 The Park – Perfect for fans of the classic Adventure Mode vibe.
 Flatlands – A blank canvas for your wildest designs.
 SandyCove Island – A picturesque getaway to spark inspiration.

And this is just the beginning! We’re already brainstorming ways to expand Creative Mode’s possibilities for the future. Stay tuned for more news! 

🎮 Remappable Controls: Play Your Way!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145962/401dba237c18c970af315a9d1277039e10ca2b9e.png
You asked, we listened! Full button remapping is now available for both keyboards and controllers. Whether you’re optimizing for comfort or your needs, the power is in your paws. We know how important this feature is to allow players to be able to experience the game fully. Now, the power is in your paws. Happy remapping everyone!

Patch Notes
✨ New Additions

 Creative Mode! Build to your heart’s content. No crafting or resources needed!
 Full Button Remapping! Customize your controls exactly how you like them.
 You can now build bouncy shrooms in both adventure and creative mode!
 Park Renaming! Second thoughts on your park’s name? Change it anytime!

🔄 Changes

 The Start Menu has been refreshed, now featuring dedicated slots for Adventure Mode and Creative Mode.
 More Save Slots! Extra room for all your parks and creations.
 Improved performance for hosts in co-op sessions when there are many buildings in the world.
 Added shadows to placement highlights when building to help with depth perception.

🐞 Bug Fixes

 Improved performance for paper lamps and candles.
 Fixed a crash when quitting the game when windows was still loading.
 Built windows and doors now load properly during startup, reducing temporary performance drops.
 Fixed Steam Deck resolution issues.
 Quest log squirrel icons now correctly match their colors in Squirrel Vision.
 Claire is now properly in focus during her dialogues.
 Fixed an issue where displayed fish used incorrect materials.
 Walls now rebuild correctly after demolishing doors and windows.
 The "Take Me to the River" achievement now unlocks as intended.
 The "Jump" mound no longer respawns after reloading the game.
 Fixed multiple acorn branches spawning on top of each other.
 Fixed squirrel animation blending issues
 Fixed camera collision with water surfaces.
 Fixed an issue where the camera could clip underwater.
 Fixed camera behavior when opening treasure chests from certain angles.
 Resolved main menu issues with credits unexpectedly exiting the game.
 Improved controller/mouse focus interactions in menus.
 Fixed so that player movement no longer continues when opening the Fish Bowl menu.
 Fixed so that the 'Back' button in various menus can now be properly clicked using the mouse.
 All building blocks are now visually highlighted when hovered over.
 Various bugs related to player camera and controller behavior during building mode have been addressed.

Amplifier Games Publisher Sale
Squirreled Away is also currently on sale. It is 35% off for another 2 days. So grab it while it lasts!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2977620/Squirreled_Away/
Thank You, Squirrels! 💛
None of this would matter without you. Keep sharing your feedback, your builds, and your love for the game and know that we’re listening!

Happy squirreling! 🐿️

notes.title: Patch 1.0.3
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145962/0286c5ccd0ef1f4278f9ab6feff6c6c3aae56589.pngHey Squirrels! 🐿️
A new patch has just landed! This time the team has focused on squashing some pesky bugs related to achievements not unlocking correctly when playing co-op with friends. We have also fixed some issues with the camera and sounds not being correct. A big thank you to everyone who reported issues and shared feedback with us. We truly appreciate your thoughts and ideas. Keep up the awesome work in our Community Hub!

Patch Notes
🔁 Changes:

 Mineable resin chunks will now respawn, and you'll find more of them scattered throughout the world.

🪲 Bug Fixes:

 “The Way of the Cache”-achievement should now unlock for every player globally upon completion.
 “Most Helpful Squirrel Ever”-achievement should now properly update for all clients.
 “Cheers!”-achievement is now individually unlockable for each player.
 “Dog Whisperer”-achievement is now unlockable individually and can be completed by clients as well.
 Food recipes now unlock and appear correctly for everyone, even after joining a game
 Fixed a bug where maps sometimes spawned underground.
 Golden Acorn pillars now correctly show collected acorns.
 Fixed an issue where clients would switch to first-person mode after the intro cutscene.
 Reduced sound range for chopping weeds, using trashcans, and trash items
 Fixed vending machine sound issues
 Cache pop-ups now show correctly for all players
 Fixed players getting stuck in floors when loading in.
 Baits no longer falsely claim to unlock things after meditating
 Replaced placeholder sound when failing Whack-a-Mole
 Canon cinematic now shows correct squirrel color
 Fixed issue with stacking pillars/beams in the same spot
 Cafe gate and walls are no longer climbable
 Moved a swimming plane so that the squirrel no longer floats above the water in the pond.
 Fixed an issue where out-of-bounds zones encroached too far into the park.
 Fixed an issue where distant evil weed sounds played across the level

notes.title: Patch Notes V.1.0.2
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145962/46463b085472ce39546894a50d827b709172d153.pngHey Squirrels! 🐿️
A new patch has just landed, fixing bugs and introducing some changes to Squirreled Away. A big thank you to everyone who reported issues and shared feedback with us. We truly appreciate your thoughts and ideas. Keep up the awesome work in our Steam Community Hub or on Discord!

Patch Notes
🔁 Changes:

 When any player in a session crafts a fur color, it will be unlocked for all players.
 When joining a server where a fur color has already been unlocked through crafting or quest completion, the color will be unlocked for that player as well.

🪲 Bug Fixes:

 No more blocked windows and doors! We’ve cleared out those pesky walls getting in the way of your view.
 Fixed a bug where climbing wasn’t functioning properly with controllers.
 Inverted Y-axis setting will now be persistent between loadings.
 If a player is too far from a chest when it's opened, they won't receive the rewards. However, they will receive them upon joining or rejoining a game where the rewards are already unlocked (still investigating other solutions).
 You can now build in every nook and cranny of the Garden Overlook property! It’s all yours to shape!.
 Fur colors unlocked by quest completion will now be available to all players, not just the completing player.
 Those toxic mushrooms won’t respawn after you’ve collected them, so you can finally breathe easy! 
 We squashed a bug that made the interact prompt act up when respawning or using "Unstuck." Now it’ll behave itself! .
 Bushes now have even occlusion settings. No more weird clipping! 
 We fixed some colliders on plank roofs, lakes, and fountains, so water now behaves like, well, water!
 Floating resin, mushrooms, and clovers? Gone! They’re back on solid ground..
 Some funky landscape near vending machines? We’ve cleaned that up!.
 Self-Chopping Mushrooms Removed.

Thank you so much for your continued support and have a great Squirreling day! 🐿️

 Fixed an issue that caused save files to become corrupted when the Daredevil quest was activated, leading to the loss of your previously built structures. Thank you for your patience as we resolved this!

Thank you to everyone who has already jumped in and started playing Squirreled Away, and for sharing your experiences with us and the community! Your feedback means a lot and helps make the game even better for everyone.

notes.title: The Journey of Squirreled Away: From Idea to Reality
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145962/1c81ff15de3dea484b28cc74ae00c705ac514da0.png
Squirreled Away is an invitation to explore, build, and unwind in a world designed to bring a sense of joy and relaxation. As we approach the game’s launch, we wanted to share some insights into how this cozy squirrel adventure came to life, the challenges we faced along the way, and what’s next for our small but passionate team.

From Idea to Squirrel Adventure
Our vision for Squirreled Away was to capture the thrill of exploration found in survival games — without the stress and danger that often comes with the genre. Instead of focusing on survival mechanics, we wanted to embrace the idea of "thrival". The idea of trying to flourish in a beautiful, cozy world.

The inspiration struck during our daily commutes, watching squirrels gracefully leap from branch to branch. The way they move, the freedom they embody, and the charm of "squirreling away" treasures in their homes felt like a perfect foundation for a game. This idea aligned perfectly with our goal: to create a stress-free world where players could explore, build, and enjoy the small moments.

How It All Started
The journey began when Per-Arne Lundberg, CEO of Amplifier Game Invest, visited our school with a unique opportunity. Amplifier was looking for a small team to take on an internship that could turn into a full-fledged studio if things went well. We brainstormed for a week, pitched Squirreled Away, and got the green light to bring it to life.

As fresh graduates, our ambition was clear: get the game across the finish line while learning as much as possible. Now, with the game’s release around the corner, we can confidently say: It’s been a wild, rewarding ride!

Challenges We Faced
Looking back, we might have made things harder for ourselves by taking on some big challenges. Here are just a few of them:


 An open-world game with no combat – We had to ensure exploration, crafting, and interactions were engaging enough without traditional combat mechanics. And open world also meant we couldn't control the way the players explore as much as it would be possible with something more linear.
 A quadruped protagonist – Animating a squirrel, especially with its complex tail movements, added significant difficulty compared to a bipedal character.
 Freedom of movement – Climbing trees, leaping between branches, and navigating the park had to feel smooth and natural, which was a massive technical challenge.
 Multiplayer functionality – Synchronizing all of these systems in a multiplayer environment took a lot of extra effort.
While these choices made development trickier, they also made the game more unique. We hope players will appreciate the love and effort that went into making Squirreled Away something special.

Where We Are Now
With the demo live on Steam and full release fast approaching, we’re in the final stretch. The last part of development is all about polish — bug fixes, refinements, and ensuring the experience feels as good as possible. We’re also paying close attention to feedback from demo players, using it to fine-tune the final version.

A Small Team, A Big Dream
Building a game as a small, relatively inexperienced team has been an adventure in itself. We couldn’t have done it without Amplifier’s incredible support, especially from our producers Dante, John, and Jojje, who brought invaluable experience and guidance. This journey has been humbling, challenging, and, above all, really fun!

It still feels surreal that we’re about to release our first game. We can’t wait for you to step into the world of Squirreled Away, explore the park, and experience the cozy adventure we’ve poured our hearts into.

Thank you for being part of this journey with us! ❤️

Wishlist the game on Steam and join us for the adventure! 🐿️

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3453320/Squirreled_Away_Demo/

notes.title: You Played, We Listened!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145962/2190dbfa4a5f30b9229515eb9de94fc3fa57a177.png

We are incredibly grateful to everyone who played the Squirreled Away demo! Your feedback and support have been invaluable in helping us refine and improve the game for the full release. In this blog, we’ll go over some takeaways from your feedback, what’s next for the full release, and how we’re making Squirreled Away even better. Let’s jump in!

Highlighted feedback from you!

We love hearing from you! Your feedback, suggestions, and even the smallest observations help shape Squirreled Away into the best game it can be. Thank you for playing and sharing your thoughts. Please keep them coming!

We’ve loved seeing your excitement around building and decorating your own treehouse with adorable items! However, we know some players have found the building system tricky, especially with mouse and keyboard. We're looking to refine the controls and add fun new blocks to make designing your dream home easier and more enjoyable. And don’t worry, the demo only scratched the surface! The full game will have many more decorations to help you make your treehouse truly your own.

Beyond that, we’re hard at work polishing the game, squashing bugs, and improving the overall experience.

During the demo, we even rolled out an update based on your feedback, adding inverted controls, ensuring strawberries respawn, introducing new building blocks, and fixing some pesky bugs.

If you enjoyed the demo and have more feedback, we’d love to hear from you! And if you have a moment, leaving a review would mean the world to us. It really helps us out.

What’s Next for Squirreled Away?

We are currently working on the full release of the game, which shouldn’t be too far off now and we are truly excited to share it with all of you! We’ve taken all your feedback to heart and are hard at work making the full game even better. With the release you will have access to explore the whole park, more fun quests and challenges and a lot more crafting tools and building blocks. And the big one, you will be able to play online with other squirrel friends! 

Closing Thoughts

From all of us at Far Seas, thank you for being part of this adventure. Your excitement and engagement mean the world to us, and we can’t wait to bring you the full experience soon. Stay tuned for more updates!

notes.title: Demo Update – Bug Fixes & Improvements!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145962/40e2fad1e6a5134bb3cbc68aace0689a7ed1868d.png

Hey everyone!

We’ve just released an update for the Squirreled Away demo, addressing some pesky bugs and making your experience smoother. Here’s what’s changed:


 Strawberries should now respawn more frequently – No more waiting around for your favorite snack!
 Fixed an issue where the player’s movement could get locked – Previously, you had to eat something or reload your save to fix it. That shouldn't be a problem anymore!
 Home sweet home, but better! We squashed some pesky building bugs and added triangle walls so you can get even more creative with your treehouse designs. 🏡✨
 Optimized visuals! The game now runs better while keeping the same cozy aesthetic. Also, colors? Even more vibrant! We love colors. 🎨🌈
 Y-axis inversion is here! Flip that camera if that’s how your squirrel brain works. We got you.
 Seagulls have been upgraded. They are just… better. You’ll see. 🦆👀


A huge thank you to everyone who has played the demo and shared their feedback! Your support means the world to us, and we’re excited to keep improving the game based on your input.

Let us know if you run into any more issues, and happy squirreling! 🐾
